original_context_note: Compared spec.full_target, H001–H006 and P with problem.md:14–41 and the entire fixed proof at lines 45–182. The ambient parameters do not encode primality, characteristic, the weight range, highest-weight-vector equations, dimension, irreducibility or admissibility; these remain explicit H. The original arbitrary-lattice quantifier, λ∈ℤ, 0≤λ<p, arbitrary characteristic-p field K, Chevalley construction at p=2, λ=0, nonzeroness and invariant-subspace conclusion are retained. No whole original H is unused. The irreducibility/highest-weight classification clause of H004 is retained although the calculation only needs its specified dimension and bracket data together with H005; it is not invoked as a classification theorem. D001–D006 retain the supplied indexing and divided-power normalization. D007 is guarded by H001; D008 is the original tensor module, not an assumed embedded lattice, and D009's multiplication map is proved injective in R002/S002 before identification with its image. D010 is guarded by N001's basis theorem. D011 is precisely the supplied coordinate module J_i; the total definition D012 uses v instead of a premature choice of a common coordinate module, and R003/S001 proves it equals every J_i using e_0=v. D013 explicitly distinguishes the complex operators from their tensor-induced restrictions and grants no lattice preservation; the requisite preservation is exported by N002. D014 retains the original integer Chevalley form and is guarded by H004. The typed constructions and their guards are available in the actual consuming packets. The supplied phases are mapped to R001 (complex coordinates), R002 (localization and matrix units), R003–R004 (coordinate module, rational rank and principal generator), R005 (both tensor identifications and reduction), R006 (irreducibility). No material proof calculation or limiting argument has been omitted; this proof has no analytic limits. All seven selected M statements were compared with successful native probes and the pinned defining source: M001 TensorProduct/Basis.lean:62–75, M002 Dimension/StrongRankCondition.lean:446–454, M003 FiniteDimensional/Lemmas.lean:253–271, M004 Dimension/Constructions.lean:269–302, M005 Dimension/Finrank.lean:113–118, M006 Data/Nat/Prime/Factorial.lean:23–42, M007 Basis/VectorSpace.lean:149–155. Their complete source conditions, including freeness/finite generation and strong rank condition where present, are retained; M001's canonical base-changed object is a typed Basis in its native definition and its displayed vector formula is the probed theorem. The earlier finrank_pi lookup is not the selected M004; the selected source is finrank_pi_fintype. No external book result is imported as E: the frozen document supplies the problem and proof, not an additional theorem root. The graph has only the six H and seven checked M roots; each N/P has its displayed unique producer, and every selected M and N lies in the actual AND closure of P. This is my author inspection, not independent Audit A or machine certification of the mathematics.

output_notes.note: Inspected the complete exported N001 against R001/S001–S004. It includes positive n and the cardinality of I, the complex basis with e_0=v, both string identities at all applicable indices, termination above λ, the endpoint x/y formulas, the h weights, and both divided-power coefficients with their zero ranges and integrality. The consumer R002 needs the actual basis and all these ranges, not the producer body; these are in N001. The induction, isolating polynomial, dimension-to-spanning application, absent next eigenvalue, and factorial normalization establish the complete output.

N002 was checked as the input used in the later packets. It now explicitly exports an R-basis indexed by I, injectivity of ι_R, complex spanning, preservation of both M and M_R by every divided power, factorial and binomial units, all three intermediate matrix-unit identities, the final word for E_ij, preservation of M_R by it, and the induced Chevalley action. R002/S002 proves the embedding/basis, S003 proves the preservation and units, and S004 computes the identities on every basis input, including the k<j and k>j cases. No later consumer needs to recover an unexported admissibility fact from H006.

The full N003 statement supplies the common J_i=J identification, nonzero finite generation, the exact unique-coordinate direct-sum description, and the dimension-one rationalization with its injective multiplication map. Its final universally quantified rational-line assertion is proved in R003/S005 and is explicitly present for R004 to use. R003/S002 gives the common-denominator injection argument, S003 supplies both maps of the rationalized coordinate equivalence, and S004 establishes n=nr, not just one bound. In particular no inference of rank one merely from J⊂ℂ is made.

R004/S001–S003 proves both existence of a nonzero b with J=Rb and the basis assertion for every such b. The minimum exponent gives an actual generator in J, since b=u_{j_0}^{-1}g_{j_0}; every other generator lies in Rb by its nonnegative exponent difference. The direct-sum uniqueness in N003 yields independence as well as spanning of b e_i. Thus N004 exports exactly the witness and basis property needed for R005, with no private valuation data escaping.

Inspected every N005 clause against R005/S001–S005: the actual map R→K, both tensor identifications, prime-field scalar action, the reduced K-basis and dimension, the identification with induced lattice operators, preserved Chevalley brackets, all reduced action and divided-power formulas, nonzero factorials for r≤λ, the reduced coordinate matrix-unit word, and its invariance consequence. R005/S003 proves the basis using M001 plus the displayed flip and first isomorphism; S004 transfers the exact matrices and operator identities; S005 proves the universal invariance implication. R006 receives basis existence and coordinate-unit invariance explicitly, rather than relying on R005's private b, A or B.

R006/S001 proves V(K)≠0 as unconditional F003. Under the arbitrary invariant subspace assumption L1, the zero case is covered and the nonzero branch L2 supplies a nonzero coordinate through F001. S002 uses every coordinate unit to put every β_i in W, obtaining W=V(K), then discharges L2 and L1 into F002. S003 universally closes W and identifies invariance under x,y,h with invariance under their K-linear span L(K). H003 supports the endpoint discussion, and the conclusion is exactly the full original nonzero irreducibility statement, without algebraic closure or distinct reduced h-weights.
